Note::TexAccessor::includes¶

Back to Note TeX Accessor API Reference

Signature¶

TokenBatch Note::TexAccessor::includes() const

Extract External Resource Targets¶

includes() extracts required path arguments from the three source commands that bring external material into a document: \input, \include, and \includegraphics. It returns the argument body, not the command spelling or outer braces. Calls from all three families remain interleaved in source order.

An optional bracket group is accepted and skipped before the required path. This is most useful for graphics options such as width, scale, or page. Both the optional group and path group must balance, and nested braces in the path are retained. Exact control-word matching prevents \inputted from being misread as \input; an escaped \\input is likewise ignored. An incomplete call contributes no partial path.

This method discovers authored targets only. It performs no filesystem access, path normalization, extension inference, recursive inclusion, or graphics rendering. That makes its result deterministic and safe for inventorying untrusted source. Use input_tags() when input commands should be replaced by visible markers in otherwise retained text, and graphics_tags() when graphics directives should become visible markers.

Because each cell can contain a different number of targets, includes() returns a closed TokenBatch. tokens() is a flat Text Note and offsets() maps each original cell to a half-open token interval. Empty cells and cells without include commands contribute repeated boundaries. Undefined input returns undefined tokens with offsets [0]; a defined non-Text Note is rejected.

The scanner is linear in source bytes and copies only extracted path bodies. It does not allocate a syntax tree or touch external storage.

Example 1: Extract All Supported Command Families¶

const auto source = pluss::make_note({
    R"(\input{chapters/{intro}} \includegraphics[width={.5\textwidth}]{plot.pdf})",
    R"(\include{appendix} \inputted{no} \\input{escaped})",
    R"(\input{unfinished)"});
const auto paths = source.tex().includes();

std::cout << paths.tokens() << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, encoding=utf8)
["chapters/{intro}", "plot.pdf", "appendix"]

The nested path braces are content and survive. Graphics options are not part of the path. The prefix collision, escaped command, and malformed group do not produce tokens.

Example 2: Recover Cell Ownership¶

std::cout << "offsets=[";
const auto offsets = paths.offsets().integers();
for (std::size_t i = 0; i < offsets.size(); ++i)
  std::cout << (i ? ", " : "") << offsets[i];
std::cout << "]\n";

Output¶

offsets=[0, 2, 3, 3]

Cell zero owns two paths, cell one owns one, and cell two owns an empty range.

Example 3: Inventory Without Performing I/O¶

for (std::int64_t i = 0; i < paths.tokens().numel(); ++i)
  std::cout << "declared: " << paths.tokens().at(i) << '\n';

Output¶

declared: chapters/{intro}
declared: plot.pdf
declared: appendix

No file is opened by this loop or by includes(); the strings are declarations found in the Note.

Example 4: Undefined And Invalid Input¶

const auto absent = pluss::Note::undefined().tex().includes();
std::cout << std::boolalpha << absent.tokens().defined() << " offsets=["
          << absent.offsets().integers()[0] << "]\n";
try {
  (void)pluss::note::make(std::vector<std::int64_t>{1}).tex().includes();
} catch (const pluss::Error&) {
  std::cout << "includes Int64: rejected\n";
}

Output¶

false offsets=[0]
includes Int64: rejected
